protocol.invalid: That is not one of the available choices. Reply with a displayed number or describe the same choice in words.

rules.numbering: Option numbers retain their displayed meaning until the state changes.
rules.yesNo: Only y, yes, 1, n, no, or 2 resolve a confirmation. Other text may resolve only when it unambiguously means the displayed choice.
rules.naturalLanguage: Natural language selects an existing state or option. It never creates, renames, reorders, or combines options.
rules.effects: Inspect before changing state, run only the operation attached to the resolved option, and verify its result before transitioning.
rules.placeholders: Only values inside braces may vary. Do not paraphrase fixed screen text.
rules.back: back returns to the state's declared back target without undoing completed work; cancel stops only the pending operation; exit invokes the exit gate.
rules.progress: For long work, render the task's fixed progress line with real status from Visum and never invent a percentage.
rules.models: Route purposes internally: Lux recognises taught identity, Vexillum locates interface elements, Peritus follows structured changes, Procurator coordinates, and Confector executes bounded actions. Do not ask ordinary users to choose editions.
rules.lockedTests: Never inspect locked-test contents before replay.
rules.authority: Installation, diagnostics opt-in, uploads, publication, destructive changes and Confector actions use their dedicated confirmation states. A prior general request is not a substitute for the displayed confirmation.

capture.permission: Screen & System Audio Recording (shown as Screen Recording on some macOS versions)

still.window: The pointer becomes a camera. Click the window to capture it, or press Escape to cancel.
still.region: Drag over the region to capture it, then release. Press Escape to cancel.

recording.screen: macOS starts a screen recording. Stop it from the menu-bar recording control or press Command-Control-Escape.
recording.window: macOS opens its capture controls for a window recording. Choose the window, start recording, then use the menu-bar recording control or Command-Control-Escape to stop.
recording.region: macOS opens its capture controls. Adjust the region, start recording, then use the menu-bar recording control or Command-Control-Escape to stop.

capture.recovery: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, enable the app or terminal running Visum, reopen it if macOS requires that, then choose Recheck permission.
